title: Identification of proteins interacting with the small GTPase Arl4D by liposome flotation assay and mass spectrometry
projectDescription: N-terminal myristoylation serves as an important modification for membrane insertion and concrete membrane anchoring of the small GTPases ADP-ribosylation factor (Arf) and ADP ribosylation factor-like (Arl). To simulate the binding topology of Arl4D on the membrane, we performed the liposome flotation assay in which N-terminally His-tagged Arl4D is loaded onto Ni-NTA-incorporated liposomes and the C-terminus of Arl4D is accessible to its interacting proteins. Liposomes containing Arl4D (active form Arl4D Q80L and inactive form Arl4D T35N) and Arl4D-interacting proteins derived from HeLa cell lysates were identified by a sucrose gradient in combination with mass spectrometry analysis. Specifically, we identified mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (Erk2) as a specific interacting protein of Arl4D Q80L. We further demonstrate a novel role for Arl4D whereby the active form of Arl4D recruits Erk1/2 to the plasma membrane and promotes Pak1 T212 phosphorylation to promote cell migration.
sampleProcessingProtocol: 1. Sample Processing Protocol The potential interaction proteins of Arl4D were prepared via liposome floating experiment. The lipids were dissolved in chloroform and mixed in the following ratio: 45% DOPC, 19% DOPE, 16% cholesterol (sheep wool), 10% PI (soybean), 5% DOPS, 5% DGS-NTA(Ni) and 0.2% NBD-labeled PE. The lipid mixture was incubated in a hot water bath for 1 hr and then rehydrated in liposome floating buffer to a final concentration of 2 mg/ml. The liposomes were then frozen and thawed in liquid nitrogen and filtered through a PC membrane with a pore size of 400 nm using a mini-extruder (Avanti Polar Lipids, Inc.). Fifty micrograms of recombinant His-Arl4D Q80L (GTP-locked form, mimic active form) or Arl4D T35N (nucleotide binding-deficient form, mimic inactive form) purified from E. coli were loaded onto 0.4 mg of NTA-incorporated liposomes and run through a 0%, 10%, and 30% sucrose gradient. The top layer containing liposomes loaded with Arl4D was mixed with 50 g HeLa cell lysates and re-suspended in a 0%, 10%, and 30% sucrose gradient to separate the Arl4D-specific interacting proteins. The resulting liposomes containing Arl4D and Arl4D-interacting proteins were subjected to one-dimensional SDS-PAGE coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analysis (GeLC-MS/MS).  2. GeLC-MS/MS analysis Proteins were separated in SDS-PAGE and gel bands in the 55-25 kDa range were excised followed by in-gel tryptic digestion as described previously (doi: 10.1073/pnas.2207414119). The peptide mixtures were extracted with acetonitrile to a final concentration of 50% and dried in a SpeedVac. For reverse-phase LC-MS/MS analysis, each peptide mixture was resuspended in HPLC buffer A (0.1% formic acid, Sigma) and loaded into a trap column (Zorbax 300 SB-C18, 0.3 × 5 mm), washed with buffer A, and the desalted peptides were then separated on a 10 cm analytical C18 column (inner diameter, 75 mm). The LC setup was coupled to a LTQ-Orbitrap linear ion trap mass spectrometry (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Full-scan MS was performed using the Orbitrap in an MS range of 400–2000 Da and intact peptides were detected at a resolution of 30,000.
dataProcessingProtocol: The resulting mass spectra were searched against the SwissProt_2023 database (Taxonomy: Homo sapiens) using the Mascot search engine (Matrix Science). To identify the proteins, the raw spectrometry data were analyzed using Proteome Discoverer software (version 1.4, Thermo Fisher Scientific). The search parameters were set as follows: trypsin as a digestion enzyme, carbamidomethylation (C) as static modification, oxidation (M), N-acetyl (protein) and Gln->pyro-Glu (N-term Q) as dynamic modification, 10 ppm for MS tolerance, 0.7 Da for MS/MS tolerance, and two for missing cleavage.
